title: Trade Unions in the European Union

abstract: Trade unions have repeatedly been challenged by neoliberal programmes implemented within Member States of the European Union (EU) and at the European level. The twentyseven country chapters at the core of this book chart the features of the neoliberal challenge in the EU Member States and the measures implemented by unions in their attempts to adapt to changed circumstances since 2000. It is clear that union activity, either independently or in conjunction with allies, will be at the centre of revitalization campaigns if the pieces left from the neoliberal challenges are to be picked up and wielded into a coherent response. This book offers a comprehensive comparative overview of the development, structure, and policies of national trade union movements in the EU. It presents an in-depth analysis of the challenges facing these organizations and their strategic and policy responses from 2000 to 2020.

narrative:
Short impact summary

Trade Unions in the European Union has reached a significant readership through open access channels, with over 2,300 downloads since publication in 2023. The work is beginning to register scholarly uptake, with one citation appearing in 2024 in the Global Labour Journal. As an early-stage publication, citation evidence remains limited, but download activity and library holdings demonstrate active engagement with the text.

Full narrative

This collaborative volume by Jeremy Waddington, Torsten Müller, and Kurt Vandaele examines trade union responses to neoliberal policy pressures across the twenty-seven member states of the European Union since 2000. Published by Peter Lang Verlag in 2023 as volume 86 of the established "Travail et Société / Work and Society" series, the book charts both the structural challenges unions have faced and the adaptive strategies they have employed. The work is positioned within debates on recession, economic policy, and labor's political-economic positioning in an era of fiscal consolidation and labor market transformation.

Reader engagement with the book is substantial in numerical terms. The open access edition hosted on the OAPEN platform has been downloaded 2,384 times, with download activity peaking in the spring months (March and April accounting for roughly 33% of annual traffic). This pattern suggests use linked to academic calendars and course preparation. The book's presence in at least three library systems globally and its classification under Economics in subject indexing indicates institutional adoption in academic and research settings.

Scholarly citations to the work are nascent but indicate relevance within labor studies. One citation has appeared to date, published in 2024 in the Global Labour Journal by Felix Syrovatka at Freie Universität Berlin. The citing article, titled "Precarious Associational Power," engages with labor movements and union studies, suggesting the book serves as a reference point for contemporary labor scholarship examining organizational power and worker representation. The citing work itself has accumulated three citations, indicating secondary resonance within the field.

The work benefits from publication within a thematic series with an established track record in labor and social policy research, positioning it alongside peer works on pension reform, austerity policy implementation, and workplace diversity. Open access availability through OAPEN and institutional repositories has lowered barriers to access, a factor likely contributing to the sustained download rate. At this early stage of the publication lifecycle, the evidence points to active reader engagement and initial scholarly recognition, with the trajectory of formal citations still developing.
